title: Restyle frontend with Tailwind CSS for a nice, fresh, modern look
description:
WHY: The app works end-to-end (photo upload, identification, Kleinanzeigen
search, pricing decision, results view, inventory) but its styling is
plain hand-written CSS (frontend/src/App.css, ~200 lines) built
incrementally across several beads with no shared design system --
functional, not "nice, fresh, modern" as requested.

HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN: adopt Tailwind CSS as the styling framework and
restyle the existing pages/components in place, without changing their
behavior, data flow, or test coverage. Sequence: install & wire up
Tailwind -> define a small shared design system (colors incl. the
existing sell/give-away/throw-away semantic colors, type scale,
spacing) as reusable Tailwind theme config -> restyle each page against
that shared system -> restyle shared chrome (nav/layout/PWA theme
color) -> remove the now-dead legacy CSS -> a final visual QA pass
(screenshots + console-error check across all pages).

EXISTING PAGES TO RESTYLE (frontend/src/):
- UploadPage.jsx -- photo capture/upload flow
- ItemResultPage.jsx -- per-item results (photo, decision badge,
  suggested price, comparable listings)
- InventoryPage.jsx -- item list with status/decision filters and
  status-transition action buttons
- App.jsx -- router root / shared nav

EXISTING SEMANTIC COLORS TO PRESERVE (from App.css, currently ad hoc --
this epic's design-tokens task should carry these into Tailwind theme
config deliberately, not invent new ones): sell = green, give_away =
blue, throw_away = red (see the decision badges visible in the
screenshots already shared with the user this session).

FLAGGED ASSUMPTIONS / OPEN QUESTIONS (not silently resolved):
1. Tailwind CSS version/setup approach (v4's CSS-first @theme config +
   Vite plugin vs. v3's tailwind.config.js) is left to the install task
   to research and pick the current recommended approach for a Vite +
   React project, documenting the choice -- don't assume a specific
   version without checking what's current.
2. Dark mode is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this epic -- "nice, fresh,
   modern" does not imply dark mode support unless the user asks
   separately. Don't add it speculatively.
3. No new npm packages beyond Tailwind and its direct build-tooling
   dependencies (e.g. the Vite plugin) -- no component libraries
   (shadcn/ui, daisyUI, etc.) unless a later task explicitly decides
   one is needed and documents why; default to plain Tailwind utility
   classes.
4. Responsive design: the app is phone-camera-first (see root README's
   "the whole point of this app is taking photos with a phone camera"),
   so mobile-width layouts are the PRIMARY target, not an afterthought
   -- each restyle task's done-criteria requires checking a mobile
   viewport (~375-420px wide), not just desktop.

DONE WHEN: all four pages/components above are restyled with Tailwind
utility classes following the shared design tokens, the legacy
App.css is removed (or reduced to only what Tailwind itself needs),
all existing frontend tests still pass unmodified in behavior, and a
final visual QA pass confirms no console errors and consistent styling
across pages via screenshots.

title: Basement Declutter App: photo -> Kleinanzeigen search -> sell/give-away/throw-away decision
description:
WHY: Personal tool to clear out a basement. User photographs an item; the
app identifies it, checks what comparable items go for on Kleinanzeigen
(German classifieds; no official public API), and recommends one of three
actions with a suggested price where relevant: (a) sell for <price>,
(b) give away, (c) throw away.

RECOMMENDED STACK (for review, not final until T1 spike resolves the
Kleinanzeigen access question):
- Backend: Python + FastAPI. Chosen over Node because the scraping
  ecosystem (httpx, BeautifulSoup, Playwright) and typical vision-API
  client libraries are strongest in Python, and it keeps one language
  across identification, scraping, and pricing logic.
- Frontend: Mobile-first PWA (React + Vite or plain HTML/JS), camera
  capture via <input capture> / getUserMedia, installable on a phone
  home screen. No native app / app-store distribution for an MVP used
  by one person.
- Vision/item identification: a vision-capable LLM (e.g. Claude with
  image input) given the photo, returning structured JSON: name,
  category, brand guess, condition guess, search keywords.
- Kleinanzeigen data access: NO official public API exists (Kleinanzeigen
  shut down third-party API access years ago). Some access method
  (scraping via Playwright, or an existing unofficial wrapper) will be
  required. This carries real ToS / bot-protection / legal-gray-area
  risk that is NOT resolved here -- see T1.
- Pricing/decision engine: simple rule-based logic over scraped
  comparable listings (e.g. median of active comparable prices), with
  configurable thresholds separating sell / give-away / throw-away.
- Storage: SQLite via SQLAlchemy/SQLModel -- single-user, single-machine
  tool, no need for a server-grade DB.
- Hosting: local machine or a small self-hosted box (e.g. home server /
  Raspberry Pi); no auth, no multi-tenancy.
- No auto-posting to Kleinanzeigen in the MVP: the app proposes a price
  and drafts a listing, but the user posts it manually. Automating
  posting is a further ToS risk and is explicitly out of scope here.

FLAGGED ASSUMPTIONS / OPEN QUESTIONS (not silently resolved):
1. Kleinanzeigen access method and its legal/ToS risk -- addressed by T1;
   nothing that depends on Kleinanzeigen data starts until T1 lands.
2. Sell/give-away/throw-away price thresholds are placeholders (e.g.
   ">EUR10 => sell, EUR0-10 with no working condition => give away,
   otherwise => throw away") -- to be revisited once real comparable
   data is available; encoded as configurable values, not hardcoded
   business logic.
3. Single user, no auth -- acceptable for a personal tool; flagged in
   case scope grows to multi-user later.
4. Vision LLM choice assumed to be Claude's vision API; swappable.

DONE WHEN: a photo uploaded through the app produces a stored Item
record with an identified name/category, a set of comparable
Kleinanzeigen listings (or an explicit "no comparables found"), a
suggested price where applicable, and one of the three recommended
actions -- visible in a results UI, with items trackable in a basement
inventory list.

title: Define a shared Tailwind design system (colors, type scale, spacing)
description:
INPUT: Tailwind CSS installed and working (prior task), and the
existing ad hoc color semantics in frontend/src/App.css -- read it
first to find the current sell/give_away/throw_away decision-badge
colors (green/blue/red) and carry the same semantic meaning forward
deliberately, not by coincidence.

ACTION: define a small, reusable design system as Tailwind theme
configuration (exact mechanism depends on the Tailwind version chosen
in the install task -- CSS-first @theme block or tailwind.config.js
theme.extend, whichever is current):
1. A semantic color palette: sell/give_away/throw_away decision colors
   (matching existing green/blue/red meaning), plus a small set of
   neutral/accent colors for general UI (background, text, borders,
   primary action buttons) that reads as "nice, fresh, modern" --
   your design judgment, keep it simple (a handful of colors, not a
   sprawling palette).
2. A type scale (heading sizes, body text) and spacing scale
   (consistent gaps/padding) -- can lean on Tailwind's sensible
   defaults, just document which scale steps this app actually uses
   so later restyle tasks are consistent rather than picking
   arbitrary values per page.
3. Document the palette/scale choices in a short reference (a comment
   block in the theme config itself is sufficient -- no need for a
   separate style-guide page/route for a personal single-user app).

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Theme config defines named tokens for at least: sell/give_away/
  throw_away semantic colors, a primary/accent color, and background/
  text/border neutrals.
- A quick smoke test (temporarily apply 2-3 of the new tokens to an
  existing low-risk element, screenshot or computed-style-assert that
  they render with the intended colors, then decide whether to leave
  that test in place or revert it -- your call, document which) proves
  the tokens are actually wired up and usable, not just declared and
  unused.
- Full existing test suite continues to pass; `npm run build` and
  `npm run lint` succeed.
- No component's actual restyle happens in this task -- that's the
  next three tasks. This task only establishes the shared tokens.
notes:
Addendum from sandbox-zlt.1 review: Tailwind's preflight reset (part of
the base Tailwind import) strips native browser styling app-wide as
soon as it's imported -- links lose their underline/color, <select>
elements lose their border/background/native arrow, and file inputs
lose their button chrome. This is expected/standard Tailwind behavior
(preflight resets everything so you style explicitly with utilities),
but it means the CURRENT (pre-restyle) app already looks visually
degraded compared to the plain-CSS baseline screenshotted earlier this
session. When defining the shared design tokens in this task, make sure
to include a base/reusable link style and a base/reusable form-control
(select, file input) style as part of the design system -- not just
colors/type/spacing -- since every restyle task downstream will need
these and they shouldn't be reinvented per-page.

close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently confirmed Tailwind v4.3.3 is genuinely the current recommended version/setup (npm dist-tags), confirmed the diff touches exactly the 4 claimed files with zero leftover changes to App.jsx/App.css/page components, reproduced the utility-class-applies proof independently in both the production build output (real generated CSS rules, no content-glob needed) and a live Chromium computed-style check, confirmed 20/20 tests pass and lint is clean. One real finding (not a done-criteria violation, but worth acting on before the restyle beads): Tailwind's preflight CSS reset already strips native link underlines, <select> chrome, and file-input button styling app-wide as soon as this lands, since it's a global reset applied before any component is restyled. title: Serve uploaded photos as static files so the results view can show the actual photo
description: INPUT: backend/app/main.py (POST /items stores photos under backend/uploads/. via UPLOAD_DIR, sandbox-yqf.4) and frontend/src/ItemResultPage.jsx (sandbox-yqf.10, currently renders an explicit placeholder instead of the real photo because there is no way to fetch it over HTTP). CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.10 confirmed there is genuinely no StaticFiles mount or /uploads route anywhere in backend/app/*.py. The bead's ACTION text said the results view should show "the uploaded photo", but this couldn't be delivered -- the done-criteria didn't explicitly require it so the bead still passed with a documented placeholder, but this is a real product gap: a "photograph an item" app whose results page can't show the photo is missing something fairly central. ACTION: 1. Backend: mount FastAPI's StaticFiles (or an equivalent explicit route) to serve files from UPLOAD_DIR at a stable path prefix (e.g. /uploads/). Make sure this does NOT allow directory traversal or listing (StaticFiles' default behavior is safe here, but verify/test it explicitly since this endpoint serves user-uploaded files back over HTTP). 2. Update Item serialization (_serialize_item in main.py) to expose a fetchable URL (e.g. photo_url derived from photo_path) rather than (or alongside) the raw filesystem path, so the frontend doesn't need to guess the URL scheme from a filesystem path. 3. Frontend: update ItemResultPage.jsx to render an using the new photo_url field instead of the placeholder, with a broken-image fallback (onError handler) in case a file is ever missing. DONE-CRITERIA: - Backend test: uploading a photo then GETting /uploads/ (or whatever the actual URL scheme ends up being) returns the image bytes with an appropriate Content-Type. - Backend test: a path-traversal-style request (e.g. /uploads/../../../etc/passwd or an encoded equivalent) does NOT escape UPLOAD_DIR -- returns 404, not arbitrary file contents. - Frontend test: ItemResultPage renders a real pointing at the new photo_url for a fixture item, and a broken-image fallback is shown if the image fails to load. - Existing backend (88) and frontend (9) tests continue to pass.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS after deep security scrutiny: instrumented Starlette's own lookup_path containment check at the source level to confirm the dynamic all_directories property changes only WHEN the directory is read, not the containment logic itself; independently reproduced the implementer's unverified 'unsafe subclass leaks a secret' claim (which had no preserved evidence) and confirmed the raw-ASGI test harness genuinely catches that class of regression (200+leak on the unsafe variant, 404 on the real one); threw a dozen traversal payload variants (encoded, double-encoded, deep, backslash, absolute-path) at the live app with zero leakage. 97/97 backend, 11/11 frontend tests pass. photo_url confirmed relative and free of filesystem structure. Minor non-blocking note: photo_path (absolute) still returned alongside photo_url, a small info leak for a single-user personal tool -- not worth a separate bead given the threat model.

title: Fix real-phone/LAN path: CORS allowlist and API base URL don't work off localhost
description:
INPUT: backend/app/main.py (CORS middleware, sandbox-yqf.5) and
frontend/src/App.jsx / .env.example (VITE_API_BASE_URL).

CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.5 found that the shipped defaults only
work when both frontend and backend are accessed via localhost. But
vite.config.js already sets server.host=true specifically so a phone on
the same LAN can reach the dev server at http://<LAN-IP>:5173 -- and the
WHOLE POINT of this app is taking photos with a phone camera while
standing in a basement. As shipped:
1. The phone's Origin header (http://<LAN-IP>:5173) is not in the
   backend's CORS allowlist (only localhost:5173/127.0.0.1:5173) ->
   browser blocks the request.
2. VITE_API_BASE_URL defaults to http://localhost:8000, which on the
   phone itself resolves to the phone, not the backend host -> even if
   CORS were fixed, the request would go nowhere.
Both currently require manual .env/CORS edits with no guidance beyond
the base-URL half already in the README.

ACTION: make LAN/real-device usage work with minimal manual
configuration:
1. Backend: make the CORS allowlist configurable (e.g. an
   ALLOWED_ORIGINS env var, comma-separated, defaulting to today's
   localhost/127.0.0.1 pair so nothing breaks for existing dev usage) OR
   auto-derive a permissive-but-still-scoped local-network rule (your
   call, document the reasoning -- avoid a blanket allow_origins=["*"]
   for a POST endpoint that writes files/DB rows unless you have a good
   reason and document the tradeoff explicitly).
2. Frontend/docs: add a clear "test from your phone" section to
   frontend/README.md covering both the CORS env var and
   VITE_API_BASE_URL needing to point at the dev machine's LAN IP, with
   a concrete example.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- A test or documented manual procedure confirming a request from a
  non-localhost origin (matching the new config) is accepted by CORS.
- README section exists with concrete LAN-IP example commands/env
  values a user can copy-paste to test from their own phone.
- Existing localhost-based dev/test workflow and full test suites
  (frontend + backend) continue to work unmodified.
close_reason: Reviewer NEEDS-WORK -> fixed directly: backend CORS implementation itself was thoroughly verified correct and robust (reproduced the full origin-matching matrix independently across 4 scenarios, ran the suite in multiple test-file orderings and 4x repeats with no flakiness, confirmed no middleware stacking across repeated reloads, confirmed allow_credentials stays False and no wildcard exists). The one real gap: README's phone-testing commands omitted 'uvicorn --host 0.0.0.0', so the backend never actually listened on the LAN interface -- confirmed against backend/Dockerfile which already does this correctly, making it a clear oversight. Fixed both occurrences directly (trivial doc fix). Also added a documented safety caveat to test_cors.py about the module-reload technique's dependency on no test-order-randomization plugin being present, per reviewer's suggestion. Re-ran suite after fixes: 88/88 still passing.

title: Kleinanzeigen search: retry with progressively looser query on zero results
description:
INPUT: backend/app/comparable_search.py (sandbox-yqf.7) and
backend/app/identification.py (sandbox-yqf.6).

CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.7 found that identification.py's vision
prompt (identification.py:92) asks the model for "2-5 short strings
suitable as search terms" -- i.e. ALTERNATIVE candidate queries a human
might try one at a time -- but comparable_search.py's _build_query
(:284-288) ANDs all of them into a single query string via
" ".join(item.search_keywords). Live, a query like "ikea
schreibtischlampe lampe schreibtisch" will very likely return zero real
comparables even when the item is genuinely resellable, which silently
biases the downstream decision engine (sandbox-yqf.8) toward
throw_away/give_away for items that would actually sell fine.

This is a quality/accuracy issue, not a correctness bug -- the current
zero-results path IS correctly implemented and tested (empty list,
status still advances to pending_decision). This bead is about making
zero real results less likely to be a false negative from over-narrow
querying.

ACTION: On a zero-results response from the first (fully-joined) query,
retry with a progressively looser query before giving up: e.g. drop the
last keyword and retry, then try only the first keyword alone, up to a
small bounded number of attempts (do not retry unboundedly -- respect
the existing rate-limiting/backoff already in comparable_search.py).
Stop retrying as soon as any attempt returns >=1 result.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Existing tests continue to pass unmodified in behavior for their
  cases (non-zero results on first try, hard failures, etc).
- New test: a fixture where the fully-joined query returns zero results
  but a looser query (e.g. first keyword alone) returns >=1 result --
  assert the service returns the non-empty result set, not an empty one.
- New test: a fixture where EVERY progressively looser query returns
  zero results -- assert the service still correctly returns an empty
  list (not an error) and Item.status still advances to pending_decision,
  same as today's zero-results behavior.
- The total number of live search calls attempted per item stays
  bounded (assert an exact upper-bound call count in the all-empty test
  case, so this can't silently become an unbounded retry loop).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently reproduced all four behaviors (non-zero-first-try = 1 call, joined-zero-then-looser-hits = 2 calls, all-zero = exactly 4 calls (cap) still advancing to pending_decision, hard-failure-on-a-looser-query aborts rather than continuing = exactly 3 calls) via its own probe script, not just reading test names. Confirmed worst-case bound empirically: 8 live calls max. Confirmed .9's pipeline tests are genuinely unaffected (they stub at the whole-service level). Ruff clean (74/74 tests pass). Non-blocking note: _build_query is now dead production code (still directly tested, harmless) -- not worth a follow-up bead for a pure cosmetic cleanup.

title: Fix enum value storage and Numeric/float type mismatch in Item/ComparableListing models
description:
INPUT: backend/app/models.py and backend/app/db.py from sandbox-yqf.3.

CONTEXT: reviewer found two real (non-blocking-for-.3, but real) issues
via mutation testing:
1. Item.decision and Item.status are stored in SQLite as the Python
   enum MEMBER NAME (e.g. "SELL", "PENDING_IDENTIFICATION"), not the
   lowercase snake_case VALUE the bead spec calls for (e.g. "sell",
   "pending_identification"). Both forms currently work on write
   because of the str-mixin, but raw SQL/exports/future Alembic
   migrations will see the wrong casing, and sandbox-yqf.4's API
   responses will likely serialize the wrong-cased value unless this
   is fixed first.
2. Item.suggested_price and ComparableListing.price are Python-typed
   as `float` (`Mapped[float]`) but the underlying column is `Numeric`,
   so reads actually return `Decimal`, not `float`. This will cause
   JSON-serialization friction (FastAPI/Pydantic) the moment
   sandbox-yqf.4 or sandbox-yqf.9 return an Item in an API response.

ACTION:
1. Fix the enum columns to store `.value` (lowercase snake_case) instead
   of `.name`, e.g. via SQLAlchemy's `Enum(..., values_callable=lambda
   e: [m.value for m in e])`, or equivalent. Existing rows: no migration
   needed for existing data since this is pre-launch/no real data yet --
   just fix the mapping going forward.
2. Fix the price/suggested_price type mismatch: either (a) change the
   column type so it genuinely round-trips as `float`, or (b) keep
   `Numeric`/`Decimal` deliberately for money-precision reasons and fix
   the Python type hints to `Mapped[Decimal]` plus decide+document how
   API beads (.4, .9) should serialize it to JSON (e.g. cast to float at
   the API boundary, or serialize as string). Pick one approach and
   document the reasoning in the same docstring location sandbox-yqf.3
   used for the migration-mechanism choice.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Existing test suite (backend/tests/) still passes unmodified in
  behavior (only touching the two issues above).
- New test: after committing an Item with decision=Decision.sell,
  querying the raw stored value via sqlite3 (or engine.execute of raw
  SQL) confirms the stored value is "sell", not "SELL". Same pattern
  for one status value.
- New test: after committing an Item/ComparableListing with a price,
  reading it back and confirming the returned Python value matches
  whichever type was chosen in step 2 above (float if (a), Decimal if
  (b)) -- and if (b), a test demonstrating the documented
  JSON-serialization approach actually produces valid JSON (e.g. via
  Pydantic model_dump_json() or json.dumps with a custom encoder, not
  just asserting no exception).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently verified via raw sqlite3 read that decision/status now store lowercase .value ('sell', 'given_away'), verified DDL changed Numeric->Float and reads return real Python float (not Decimal), confirmed via baseline diff (40 vs 42) that the fix is purely additive with zero pre-existing assertions weakened, and confirmed enum member names/values themselves are unchanged (only DB column mapping changed). All 30 tests from sandbox-yqf.6/.7 still pass against the changed models -- no regression.

title: Pricing & sell/give-away/throw-away decision engine
description:
INPUT: an Item with its associated ComparableListing rows (from the
search module).

ACTION: Implement decision logic:
- Compute a suggested_price from comparable listings (e.g. median of
  active comparable prices; document the exact formula chosen).
- Classify into one of three decisions using configurable thresholds
  (not hardcoded magic numbers -- read from a config module/file):
  a) sell: median comparable price >= SELL_THRESHOLD (placeholder
     default e.g. EUR10, per epic assumption #2)
  b) give_away: below SELL_THRESHOLD but item condition is usable /
     comparables exist at low price
  c) throw_away: no comparables found AND/OR item condition indicates
     broken/unusable
- Update the Item row: suggested_price, decision, status=decided.

OUTPUT: decision engine + tests.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Unit test: comparables with median price above threshold ->
  decision=sell with correct suggested_price.
- Unit test: comparables present but below threshold, item usable ->
  decision=give_away.
- Unit test: zero comparables and/or condition=broken -> decision=
  throw_away.
- Thresholds are read from a single named config location, verified by
  a test that changing the config value changes the classification
  boundary.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently re-derived all done-criteria in a fresh test file (not reading the implementer's tests) -- median computation, threshold boundary inclusivity, monkeypatch-both-directions threshold test, condition=broken always winning over high comparables, and a real SQLite round-trip confirming no regression of the sandbox-yqf.14 enum fix. Zero-comparables->throw_away judgment call confirmed as a defensible reading of the bead text, documented in code not just chat. Fixed one cosmetic lint nit (unused import) myself. Pinned a real integration note into sandbox-yqf.9: decide_item doesn't check incoming status, so .9 must only call it once status has genuinely reached pending_decision.

title: Pipeline orchestration: photo -> decision end-to-end + GET /items/{id}
description:
INPUT: the upload endpoint, identification service, search module, and
decision engine, all already implemented.

ACTION: Wire the four steps into a single pipeline triggered after photo
upload (in-process sequential calls is sufficient for this scale; no
message queue needed): upload -> identify -> search -> decide, updating
Item.status at each stage. Add `GET /items/{id}` returning the full Item
record including its comparable listings, suggested price, decision, and
current status (so a client can poll while the pipeline runs, or fetch
after it's synchronously done -- pick synchronous execution within the
upload request unless that risks request timeouts, in which case run it
as a background task and document the polling contract).

EDGE CASES: if any pipeline stage fails (per that stage's documented
failure behavior), GET /items/{id} must still return a valid response
showing the stage the item is stuck at, not a 500.

OUTPUT: orchestration code + `GET /items/{id}` endpoint + tests.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Integration test: uploading a fixture photo (with identification and
  search mocked/stubbed) results in a fetchable Item via GET /items/{id}
  showing decision, suggested_price, and comparable listings populated
  end-to-end.
- Integration test covers a stage failure (e.g. mocked search failure)
  and asserts GET /items/{id} still returns 200 with a status reflecting
  where the pipeline stalled, not a crash.
notes:
Addendum from sandbox-yqf.6 review (identification service):
1. ItemIdentificationService.identify_item mutates the Item ORM object
   in place but deliberately does NOT commit a DB session -- this
   task (.9, pipeline orchestration) owns the session and must commit
   after calling it, or the identification results won't persist.
2. identify_item returns a bool indicating success/failure. .9 must
   check this return value -- on False (API failure), leave the
   pipeline at status=pending_identification for retry rather than
   silently proceeding to the search step as if identification
   succeeded.
Addendum from sandbox-yqf.8 review (decision engine):
PricingDecisionService.decide_item does NOT check the incoming
Item.status before classifying -- it will happily classify an item
still stuck at pending_search (e.g. because sandbox-yqf.7's search
step failed/exhausted retries) as throw_away, since it just sees
"zero comparables" with no way to distinguish "genuinely searched,
found nothing" from "search never actually completed". This
orchestration task (.9) must guard the pipeline ordering itself: only
call decide_item once status has actually reached pending_decision
(i.e. the search step succeeded, even if it succeeded with zero
results) -- do not call it on an item still at pending_search.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: 68/68 tests pass, ran the pipeline test file 5x for flakiness (none found). Critical check -- ran a REAL uvicorn server (not just TestClient) with 10 concurrent uploads to verify the BackgroundTasks threading model doesn't break SQLite; zero threading/locking errors, confirmed check_same_thread=False from db.py plus a fresh per-thread session in run_pipeline_with_new_session makes this safe. Both mandatory integration requirements (commit+check identify_item's bool; only call decide_item once status reaches pending_decision) verified as real code at specific line numbers, not just test assertions. Ruff clean (implementer's 'no linter' claim was wrong -- ruff exists and reviewer ran it). Fixed a docstring typo myself.

ACTION: Implement a backend service that sends the item's photo to a

Use Claude's vision API as the default provider (per epic's flagged

OUTPUT: search module + tests using recorded/fixture HTML or mocked

Addendum from sandbox-yqf.1 spike review (docs/kleinanzeigen-access.md),

1. sort_type: use "DATE_DESCENDING" (newest first), NOT

ValueError-wrapping for unresolvable locations), condition extraction from the library's localized attributes dict confirmed genuine (not stubbed), retry-once and zero-results edge cases both correctly implemented and tested, FK persistence verified via ad-hoc session. One real but non-blocking design concern (query-joining of alternative search terms likely yields spurious zero-results live) filed as sandbox-yqf.15.

title: Derive stored upload extension from sniffed image format, not client-supplied header/filename
description:
INPUT: backend/app/main.py's upload endpoint (sandbox-yqf.4, hardened in
sandbox-yqf.16) -- specifically _pick_extension.

CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.16 found a narrow, currently
UNEXPLOITABLE edge case while stress-testing the magic-byte sniffing:
_pick_extension prefers mimetypes.guess_extension(content_type) for the
stored filename's extension, falling back to the client-supplied
filename's suffix for unrecognized image/* content-types. A file with
valid JPEG magic bytes at the start but SVG body content, served with
an unusual content-type like "image/x-weird", would pass the sniff
(bytes start with real JPEG magic) but get stored with a ".svg"
extension (from the client filename), which StaticFiles would then
serve with an SVG content-type.

Reviewer confirmed this is NOT currently exploitable: such a file
cannot simultaneously satisfy the JPEG magic-byte check (which only
requires the FIRST few bytes) and be well-formed SVG/XML (parsing fails
at column 0-4 in the tested cases), so browsers abort rendering before
any embedded script could run. This bead is defense-in-depth, not a
live vulnerability fix.

ACTION: derive the stored file's extension from the SNIFFED image
format (the magic-byte check that already ran and passed) rather than
from the client-supplied Content-Type header or filename -- e.g. if the
sniff matched the JPEG signature, always store as .jpg regardless of
what the client claimed. This removes the extension-mismatch class of
issue entirely rather than relying on "well-formed XML" being
coincidentally hard to also start with valid raster magic bytes.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- _pick_extension (or its replacement) uses the sniffed format, not
  Content-Type/filename, to choose the stored extension.
- Existing upload tests continue to pass.
- New test: a file with valid JPEG magic bytes, an unusual/absent
  Content-Type, and a client-supplied filename ending in a different
  extension (e.g. ".svg" or ".txt") is stored with a .jpg extension
  matching its sniffed format, not the claimed one.

title: docker-compose.yml doesn't bind-mount backend/tests, so container tests go stale

`./backend/app:/app/app` mount in docker-compose.yml's backend service.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- docker compose config shows the new tests bind mount resolved

- README (or a code comment) notes that docker compose run --rm backend

title: Add regression test coverage for ItemResultPage polling and stuck-state logic
description:
INPUT: frontend/src/ItemResultPage.jsx (sandbox-yqf.10).

CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.10 had to write and run its own
throwaway test (since deleted, not committed) to empirically verify the
polling behavior (fetch count grows while non-terminal, freezes on
terminal status, stops on unmount via AbortController+clearInterval)
and the MAX_POLL_MS "taking longer than expected" stuck-state path --
neither is covered by a committed test, so a future change could
silently break either with nothing catching it. Also flagged: the sell
test asserts link/href for comparable listings but not the actual
rendered price/condition/location text for each listing.

ACTION: add committed tests (Vitest, fake timers where appropriate) for:
1. Polling continues (fetch called repeatedly) while status is
   non-terminal, and stops immediately once status becomes terminal.
2. Polling/fetching stops on component unmount (no further fetch calls
   after unmount).
3. The MAX_POLL_MS stuck-state message appears if status is still
   non-terminal after the configured timeout.
4. The sell-case comparable listing rendering asserts the actual
   displayed price/condition/location text, not just the link/href.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- All four behaviors above have a passing, committed test.
- Temporarily reverting the relevant behavior in ItemResultPage.jsx
  (e.g. removing the clearInterval cleanup, or the MAX_POLL_MS check)
  causes the corresponding new test to fail -- confirms the tests
  actually catch regressions, not just pass trivially.

title: Fix vacuous disabled-state assertion in App.test.jsx
description:
INPUT: frontend/src/App.test.jsx (sandbox-yqf.5).

CONTEXT: reviewer found that the in-flight-disable test at
App.test.jsx:41 (expect(input).toBeDisabled()) runs AFTER the mocked
fetch has already resolved, so it's checking a stale/detached node's
last-rendered attribute rather than genuinely proving the input is
disabled DURING the request. The reviewer independently proved the real
component behavior IS correct (via a deferred-promise probe: disabled
mid-flight, re-enabled after), so this is a test-quality gap, not a
product bug.

ACTION: rewrite the in-flight assertion using a deferred/controllable
mock fetch (e.g. a Promise that doesn't resolve until the test
explicitly resolves it) so the test genuinely observes `disabled=true`
WHILE the request is pending, then resolves the mock and confirms the
input re-enables (or the success state renders). Also add a test that a
second file-selection/submit attempt while a request is already in
flight does not fire a second fetch call (currently untested per the
review).

DONE-CRITERIA:
- New/rewritten test fails if the disabled-during-flight behavior is
  removed from App.jsx (verify this by temporarily removing the disable
  logic and confirming the test catches it, then restoring it).
- Test asserting duplicate-submission prevention exists and passes.
- Full frontend test suite continues to pass.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently reproduced the regression-proof (removed disabled-during-flight logic, confirmed both new tests fail; restored, confirmed 20/20 pass). Confirmed the disabled-state assertion genuinely runs before the deferred fetch resolves, not after. Went further than the bead asked on the duplicate-submission test: isolated the fetch-call-count assertion from the disabled-state assertion and confirmed it independently catches loss of the guard, proving the test exercises real app behavior (disabled is app output, fetch count is app behavior) not just testing-library's no-op-on-disabled-input library behavior. Scope clean (UploadPage.test.jsx only, +84/-4). 20/20 frontend, 132/132 backend unaffected. No follow-up beads needed -- the one design note raised (no app-level early-return guard beyond the disabled attribute) was judged adequate, not a gap, for a file input.

title: Upload endpoint: case-insensitive content-type check + reject SVG/sniff magic bytes
description: INPUT: backend/app/main.py POST /items (sandbox-yqf.4). CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.4 found two minor gaps in the non-image-rejection check at main.py:113: 1. The content-type comparison is case-sensitive, so a technically valid "IMAGE/JPEG" header (HTTP media types are case-insensitive per RFC 9110) would be wrongly rejected with 400. Unlikely from browsers but worth fixing for correctness. 2. image/svg+xml and image/heic are accepted with no magic-byte sniffing (only Content-Type header is checked). An SVG can contain embedded
close_reason: Reviewer PASS with 20 independent adversarial probes: confirmed magic-byte signatures are real compound checks (not first-byte/substring), confirmed uppercase/mixed-case/charset-suffixed Content-Type all accepted, confirmed the critical case -- SVG bytes mislabeled as image/jpeg/png/webp/heic all correctly rejected, defeating a lying header. Probed a polyglot residual risk (JPEG magic bytes + SVG body) and concluded via actual XML-parse-failure analysis it is not exploitable (browsers abort SVG rendering on parse error), not just assumed safe. Confirmed graceful handling of truncated/empty payloads, correct 413-vs-400 ordering, zero leftover files/rows across five rejection paths, and purely-additive test diff (84 lines added, 0 deleted). One lightweight follow-up filed: sandbox-yqf.23 (derive stored file extension from sniffed format rather than header/filename, for defense-in-depth against the narrow unexploitable-today edge case the reviewer found).

title: docker-compose bind mounts miss frontend config files (index.html, vite.config.js, package.json)
description:
Found during review of sandbox-yqf.2. docker-compose.yml only bind-mounts
./frontend/src and ./frontend/public into the frontend container, so
editing frontend/index.html, frontend/vite.config.js, or
frontend/package.json on the host won't be reflected without a rebuild.
Minor DX nit, not blocking. Fix: mount the whole ./frontend directory
(excluding node_modules via a named volume or .dockerignore) or add the
missing files individually.
DONE-CRITERIA: editing frontend/index.html on the host and refreshing
the dev server (already running via docker compose up) shows the change
without a container rebuild.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: confirmed docker compose config validates and resolves the frontend mounts exactly as claimed (bind ./frontend->/app + volume->/app/node_modules), confirmed the volume-overlay precedence reasoning is correct standard Docker behavior, confirmed Vite's dev server (npm run dev) watches the bind-mounted filesystem so host edits would be reflected without rebuild, confirmed the honesty of the 'no live docker daemon here' disclosure (checked docker.sock/docker ps directly), confirmed scope stayed to docker-compose.yml only. Config-level verification is the ceiling of what's checkable in this sandbox (no daemon, CDN egress blocked) and the bead was judged fairly against that constraint.

title: backend Dockerfile doesn't copy tests/, so docker compose run backend pytest fails
description:
Found during review of sandbox-yqf.2. backend/Dockerfile only COPYs the
app/ directory, not tests/, so pytest can't run inside the built
container image (only natively, which is what the current README
documents -- so this isn't breaking anything documented today, but it's
a latent gap if someone expects `docker compose run backend pytest` to
work).
DONE-CRITERIA: `docker compose run backend pytest` (or equivalent) passes
inside the container, OR the README explicitly documents that container
test execution isn't supported and native pytest is required.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: reproduced both the bug and the fix via isolated filesystem simulations of the actual docker build output -- before the fix, pytest collected 0 items (exit 5, confirming the bug was real); after, 128 passed matching the native run exactly. Confirmed the .dockerignore exclusion was genuinely removed (not commented/replaced), confirmed no new deps needed, confirmed pytest.ini inclusion is correct though not strictly required, confirmed README command syntax is accurate. One follow-up filed: sandbox-yqf.22 (docker-compose.yml still doesn't bind-mount backend/tests, so container tests go stale until rebuild -- same class of gap .12 just fixed for frontend).

title: Basement inventory list + manual status tracking
description:
INPUT: the pipeline orchestration and Item model.

ACTION:
- Backend: `GET /items` (list, filterable by status/decision query
  params) and `PATCH /items/{id}/status` to manually transition status
  to listed | given_away | disposed (user confirms they acted on the
  app's recommendation -- no automated posting to Kleinanzeigen, per
  epic assumption/decision).
- Frontend: inventory list view showing all items with photo thumbnail,
  decision, status, and a control to advance status (e.g. "Mark as
  listed on Kleinanzeigen", "Mark as given away", "Mark as disposed"),
  plus filters by status/decision.

EDGE CASES: reject invalid status transitions (e.g. jumping straight
from pending_identification to disposed) with a 400 and a clear message
listing valid next states from the current one.

OUTPUT: endpoints + UI, committed.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Backend tests: GET /items respects status/decision filters; PATCH
  /items/{id}/status succeeds for valid transitions and returns 400 with
  the correct message for an invalid one.
- Manual test or component test confirms the UI list renders items
  grouped/filterable by status and the status-advance controls call the
  PATCH endpoint correctly.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: exhaustively verified all 49 (7x7) status-transition pairs individually (every valid edge succeeds and persists, every invalid pair 400s with current+valid-next-states message, unmutated), reproduced the full GET /items filter matrix (status/decision/both/neither/non-matching/bad-enum), confirmed the ItemResultPage.test.jsx change is a single proportionate line-count bump matching a genuinely new nav link (nothing else weakened), and confirmed frontend status-advance buttons are correctly gated so no button can ever produce a 400. 128/128 backend, 18/18 frontend tests pass. No regression in pipeline/identification/search/pricing internals. This closes out the epic's core feature set -- photo upload through inventory tracking is now fully wired end-to-end. One follow-up filed: sandbox-yqf.21 (transition table duplicated in JS with a real drift risk).

title: Frontend: item results view
description:
INPUT: GET /items/{id} endpoint.

ACTION: Build a results page showing: the uploaded photo, identified
name/category, the recommended decision (sell/give-away/throw-away)
rendered clearly, the suggested price (when decision=sell), and a list
of the comparable Kleinanzeigen listings with clickable links to the
original listings.

OUTPUT: working page, committed.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Manual test or component test against a seeded/fixture Item (one per
  decision type: sell, give_away, throw_away) confirms the correct
  elements render for each case, including the comparables list for the
  sell case.
- Page handles a "still processing" status by showing a pending state
  rather than breaking on missing fields.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently verified routing split preserves .5's upload flow verbatim (diffed against the prior commit -- disabled-during-flight, error handling, retry, all intact), confirmed the photo-servability gap claim is accurate (no StaticFiles route anywhere in backend), confirmed suggested_price gating (decision=sell only) is a deliberate correct choice by reading pricing.py directly (a throw_away item CAN have a non-null price from working comparables, hiding it is correct not lossy), and empirically proved the polling logic (wrote and ran its own throwaway timer-based test: fetch count grows, freezes on terminal status, stops on unmount). 9/9 frontend tests pass, 88/88 backend unaffected. Two real gaps filed: sandbox-yqf.19 (no static file serving for uploaded photos -- the one ACTION item not literally delivered, though done-criteria didn't require it) and sandbox-yqf.20 (no regression test for polling/stuck-state logic, which reviewer had to verify by hand).

title: Frontend: photo capture/upload page
description:
INPUT: the photo upload endpoint (POST /items).

ACTION: Build a PWA page with a camera-capture/file-picker input
(<input type=file capture>) that lets the user take or choose a photo
and submits it to POST /items, then navigates to a "processing" state
showing the returned item id.

EDGE CASES: show a user-visible error message if the upload fails
(network error or 4xx/5xx from the backend); disable the submit control
while the request is in flight to prevent duplicate submissions.

OUTPUT: working page, committed.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Manual test (documented with steps + screenshot or terminal output in
  the task summary) or component test: selecting a fixture image and
  submitting successfully creates an item via the real or mocked backend
  and the UI shows the returned item id.
- Error path manually verified: a forced backend failure surfaces a
  visible error message rather than failing silently.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: verified field-name match against the real backend endpoint at source (not summary), confirmed the in-flight disable is genuinely wired via a deferred-promise probe, confirmed CORS addition is minimal/correctly scoped (no wildcard, no credentials), confirmed 74/74 backend tests still pass, confirmed a 5xx-with-non-JSON-body edge case also surfaces a clear error. Auto-submit-on-select judged within the bead's literal intent. Two non-blocking follow-ups filed: sandbox-yqf.17 (vacuous disabled-state test assertion) and sandbox-yqf.18 (real-phone/LAN path doesn't work as shipped -- CORS allowlist and API base URL both need LAN-aware config).
